title: Pressure-cooker butternut squash soup
subtitle: Silky, smooth, and ready in 15 minutes
excerpt: Butternut squash with onion and ginger cooked under pressure and blended into a smooth, velvety soup. The pressure cooker brings the squash to fully tender in 8 minutes and produces an exceptionally smooth result after blending.
sourceNotes: Butternut squash soup became common in British cooking in the 1990s as squash became more widely available. The combination with ginger and spices follows the approach seen across British and American recipe literature from that period.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool and freeze in airtight containers for up to 4 months. Reheat gently over medium heat.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Freeze in individual portions.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps refrigerated for up to 4 days. Reheat with a splash of stock.

content.text: Pressure-cooker butternut squash soup is silky and smooth. The squash cooks so thoroughly under pressure that it blends into a fine purée in under a minute. The 8-minute cook is faster than roasting. It also gives a deeper, more concentrated flavour than boiling.
Ginger adds warmth without heat. For a spiced version, add cumin and coriander with the ginger. For a plainer version with sweeter squash flavour, use only thyme.
Peeling butternut squash is the most laborious part of this recipe. A sharp peeler works well; alternatively, cut the squash in half, scoop out the seeds, and peel each half before dicing.

items.prepNote: about 1 kg, peeled, deseeded, and diced into 4 cm chunks

content.text: Set the pressure cooker to sauté or use the open pot on the hob. Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, and cumin; stir for 1 minute. Add the squash chunks and {{stock-vegetable}} of vegetable stock. Season with salt and pepper.

Seal the lid and bring to high pressure. Cook at high pressure for 8 minutes. Quick-release the pressure. Open the lid, the squash should be very soft. Use a stick blender to blend directly in the pot until completely smooth. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Add a splash of hot stock if too thick.

rows.cause: Squash varies in water content, dryer squash absorbs more stock.
rows.fix: Stir in additional hot stock in 50 ml increments until you reach a pourable consistency.

rows.symptom: The soup is not smooth despite blending
rows.cause: The squash was not fully cooked, or the stick blender was not given enough time.
rows.fix: Blend for a full minute. If any lumps remain, return to pressure for 3 minutes and blend again.

content.text: Butternut squash soup is autumn and early winter cooking, made when squash is at its best and the weather has turned. It is an excellent soup for batch cooking: a double batch freezes well and can be reheated from frozen in a saucepan with minimal effort. Finish each bowl with a swirl of double cream or a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of smoked paprika.
